# NOTES: TWO BOOKS

## BOOK 1: The Boys of Grand Pré School (James De Mille; Gutenberg 56232)

**Chars:** B.O.W.C. ("Bee-Oh-Double-You-See", secret club: Bart, Bruce Rawdon, Arthur Rawdon, Phil, Tom). Solomon (Black cook, "Grand Panjandrum", dialect, "Bee See Double"). Capt. Corbet (old sailor, meek, mineral rod, wife Mrs. Corbet, baby, schooner Antelope). Mr. Long (teacher, eloquent, defends Corbet). Mr. Simmons (teacher). Dr. Porter (principal, antiquarian, museum). Pat (Irish, attic room). Jiggins, Bogud, David Digg, Billymack, Johnny Blue, Muckle, Sammy Ram Ram (other boys). Gaspereaugians (rival valley boys). Old Zeke (witness, drunk). Pieter Schwab (Dutch justice of peace). Captain Pratt (jovial, salvages Antelope). Bennie Grigg (Scott's Bay fisherman). Mr. Smalley, Mr. Atkins (named, not met).

**Places:** Grand Pré Academy on hill; Old French Orchard (cellars); Gaspereaux valley; Mud Creek; Blomidon; Minas Basin; Cornwallis; North Mountain; Horton Bluff; Parrsboro, Pratt's Cove, Five Islands; Scott's Bay; Hall's Harbor; Cape Split; Ile Haute; Ridge Road; Boarding House; the camp in the woods (dam, pool, jaw of big fish over door).

**Ch I – Camp in Woods.** Last day of spring recess. Solomon brings lunch, leaves. Weapons debated (clubs, crackers, boomerangs, lassos, cannon); settle on bows, arrows, whistles. Captain Corbet appears ("Who goes there?"). Shows junk from pockets (list incl. "Bonaparte's Oraculum", brass cannon, rat skin). Holds "mineral rod" (slender dirty stick), says it found a buried pot of gold in an old French cellar. Shows copper coin: LOUIS XIV ROI DE FRANCE. Says rod "turned down hard" at one spot; other cellar didn't. Bart cites Benedict Bellefontaine, wealthiest farmer of Grand Pré. Goes to Old French Orchard.

**Ch II – Old French Orchard.** View from hill (Academy, dikes, Horton Bluff, Basin, Blomidon). Acadian history: 2000 expelled from Grand Pré; Evangeline cited. Corbet walks cellar; rod falls at centre. Boys plan dig. Bart's "Book of Magic": lights in multiples of 3 or 7, midnight to cock-crow, silence. Bruce superstitious, hides fear. Plan: dig that night, last holiday night, with Solomon as Grand Panjandrum.

**Ch III – Deed of Darkness.** Midnight. 21 lights (lanterns, pails, kettles); the Bust placed by woods. Tools: pickaxe, four spades. Bart lights candles. Corbet "solemn", pines for baby. Incantations: Phil (English history), Tom (Euclid), Arthur (Arnold's Latin), Bruce (Latin declensions), Bart (Caesar). Corbet objects ("heathen"), demands English; Bart's hymn to tune "Rousseau's Dream" ("Why did we deprive the Frenchman..."; "pot of gold"). Bruce digs with pickaxe, strikes metal ("ringing, metallic"). Then a sudden hideous roar. Panic; lights blown out. Solomon flees, barricades room, hides till dawn. Corbet cries "O, my babby!" and runs. All boys flee. Bruce, shamed, turns back: "I'll go back to that hole, if I die for it." All return, relight, decide to fill hole. Corbet returns: "vice o' warnin"; snaps mineral rod across knee, says it came from "old Zeke"/a demon-man; gives up gold.

**Ch IV – Stone Wall.** Sunrise description. Mr. Long needs stones back (wall taken for Antelope ballast; owner vowing vengeance). Reward: rest of week's holidays. Boys rebuild wall, better than before. Mud Creek: Antelope on her side in mud, masts down. Corbet on wall: "No go... that there schooner's a gone sucker." Blames baby ("the infant called me off"). Corbet served a writ by wall-owner; Mr. Long promises defence ("I'll pay the damages").

**Ch V – Mystery of the Garret.** Night howls/knocks in attic above Rawdons' room; cupola; Pat's room beside attic. Boys search, find nothing. Jiggins, Bogud alarmed; Pat fuels rumours. Bart suspects Pat. Bart spends day in attic, reveals nothing.

**Ch VI – The Trial.** Hall; justice Pieter Schwab (short, fat, bald, Dutch accent). Suit: $500 damage to potato field. Witness Old Zeke ("was it a horse? cow? rat?"). Mr. Long cross-examines prosecutor: one acre, ~100 bushels, ~$40 value. "Old Zeke's rat." Boys testify Corbet was home nursing baby. Long's speech; "nursing... his baby!" Case dismissed; prosecutor pays costs. Corbet heroized.

**Ch VII – Gaspereaux.** Next day: noises again. Bart stays behind, to meet at camp at 4. Boys fish Gaspereaux (Phil 7 trout, Bruce 4, Arthur 3, Tom 5); roast trout, no salt. Walk back through Grand Pré village bridge; no Gaspereaugians. At camp: Gaspereaugians (enemies, town vs gown) waiting.

**Ch VIII – Ambush.** Bart and Solomon ambushed by ~30 Gaspereaugians; tied; Solomon's basket of food seized. Bart jokes; mentions snowball that blacked eye. Bart slips his bonds, frees Solomon. Bruce confronts: "What are you doing here?" Big Gaspereaugian challenges Bruce to wrestle; Bruce gets underhold, lifts him, dumps him into pool. Gaspereaugians leave ("Exeunt omnes Gaspereaugienses!"). Bart & Solomon reach camp with basket. Bart: "sixteen minutes after four."

**Ch IX – Donkey.** Lunch at camp. Distant roar again. Bart: Gaspereaugians not guilty. Boys go to Dr. Porter's pasture. Donkey (bought from "ole scissa grinda" for children) brays; mystery solved; boys laugh. Solomon's joy/laughter. Solomon: "I'm a fessa ob de cool an airy 'partment" (kitchen). Boys resolve to dig again by daylight.

**Ch X – Ploughshare.** Boys get spades, pickaxe at Academy. Dig at hole; strike iron; lid loose. Lift: rusty old ploughshare. Boys mock. Also found: colter, bolts, ox chain, iron pot, nails, spikes, 13 copper sous ("UN SOU"), bone (Bart claims human, Phil says horse). Joke: "archaeologists".

**Ch XI – Museum.** Boys dump relics on Dr. Porter's study table (ruin Euripides, Hebrew Lexicon, Longinus, Quarterlies, blotting pad). Doctor laughs uncontrollably; family joins. Doctor, enthusiastic antiquarian, delighted. Mr. Simmons, Mr. Long summoned. Bart tells whole story, comic.

**Ch XII – Blomidon Excursion.** Doctor proposes Saturday trip to find French fort on Blomidon; 3 double wagons, 6 horses; start 4am. Drive through Cornwallis; breakfast on North Mountain; view of Grand Pré, Academy. Doctor's history: Port Royal 1606; Utrecht 1713; Neutrals; oath proviso; Halifax 1749; Braddock defeat; Acadian expulsion; schooners from Boston (Apthorp & Hancock bills); Longfellow's Evangeline.

**Ch XIII – Lost in Woods.** Hike into forest left of Blomidon; ox-trails, fallen trees, moss, "Barrens" (fireweed, blueberries). Fog descends. Doctor silent: realizes he's lost. Reach cliff edge over surf.

**Ch XIV – Pat and the Porcupine.** Doctor's map: Hall's Harbor. Bruce: "everyone swerves to the right." Party splits: Bruce leads Scott's Bay party (Bart, Arthur, Tom, Phil, Pat); doctor leads Hall's Harbor party (Jiggins, Bogud, Sammy, Johnny Blue, Billymack). Pat leads with straight pole; hits porcupine; chases it; vanishes. Boys search, shout, give up.

**Ch XV – Pat Returns.** Dusk. Boys find snake fence, road. Pat returns: "wild turkey... wild goose with fower legs" = porcupine. Bart: "real ghost". Pat: porkypine.

**Ch XVI – Scott's Bay.** ~8pm. Two parties meet on road; doctor's party lost too. Doctor: Bruce right; circled; now at Scott's Bay. Hear surf inland; ask at cottage; Bennie Grigg (red-faced, stocking feet, pipe): "This here place is Scott's Bay!"

**Ch XVII – Hospitality.** Mrs. Bennie. Huge spread (broiled salmon, ham, mince pies, alewives, buckwheat pancakes, maple honey, johnny cakes, etc.). Sleep: doctor room; Jiggins/Bogud settee; Sammy/Johnny floor; rest hayloft. Scott's Bay description (500 people, Cape Split, Ile Haute). Sunday: doctor preaches; admits error, advises never trust doctor of divinity in woods. Monday 4am walk to horses; back at Grand Pré ~11am; school delayed, extra holiday. "Hurrah, boys!"

**Ch XVIII – Solomon's Supper.** Pat frightens small boys (Harry Thompson pale). Bart plans to stop it. Last holiday night supper in Rawdons' rooms; Solomon's speech. Knock at door (Pat's doing); bell toll. Solomon flees. Boys search attic, cupola. Bruce finds string tied to bell tongue, leads to Pat's room. Bruce jerks string free (Pat's "ghost" string lost).

**Ch XIX – Donkey Plan.** Bart: "The donkey's the very man." Boys lead donkey upstairs with carpet-bound feet, turnips; Jiggins sees donkey; Bogud calls out. Donkey left in garret near Pat's room. Pat rings bell; donkey brays; Pat leaps, tears downstairs, locks himself in Bart's room.

**Ch XX – Revelation.** Pat confesses. Owl (Mr. Slocum's escaped screech owl, from cupola window) was screeching; Pat pranked. Solomon: "Mas'r Owl... I'se gwine to bile him"; Pat gives meat to owl. Owl returned to Mr. Slocum (2 miles away). Summoned to Mr. Long's study.

**Ch XXI – Wigging.** Mr. Long rebukes harshly; Bart protests; Pat confesses fully. Long relaxes. Captain Corbet enters with baby, wanting Long to hold it; Long hurries out; Corbet sulks ("I felt it sore"). Dr. Porter: bone was "horse or cow" (Simmons says cow). Museum ceremony: Bruce speech (pot, plough, bone = "nightmare's bone"), three cheers. Bart's poem "THE TRUE THEORY OF THE BONE" (Parley Yoo; leg shot by Britisher; buried under apple tree). Relics left in Museum.

**Ch XXII – Louisbourg.** Doctor's lecture: Acadian exile by Boston schooners; Pelitcodiac and St. John River incidents. First siege of Louisbourg 1745: Shirley, Pepperell (merchant-colonel), Major Vaughn, thirteen men in Royal Battery ("by grace of God and courage of thirteen men"); "L'audace, l'audace toujours l'audace." Second siege a British blunder. Boys visit Antelope; Captain Pratt appears: "Wal, whar's Corbet?"

**Ch XXIII – Antelope Raised.** Pratt: schooner not lost; will raise. Tackle on spars; boys pull; "Up she rises; Hi ho, cheerly, men!" Schooner rights. Corbet to be surprised.

**Ch XXIV – Corbet's Exile.** Pat sent to fetch Corbet ("testimonial"). Pat tries to keep baby; disaster; Mrs. Corbet arrives, Pat flees. Corbet shown Antelope; weeps; "Boys, adoo!" Sails with potatoes to Boston; crew: Wade (mate), Gipson. Boys wave; Antelope enters fog bank.

## BOOK 2: Adele Doring at Boarding-School (Grace May North; Gutenberg 62360)

**Chars:** Adele Doring (14; "Della"; rose tam; brother Jack; "Mumsie", "Giant Daddy"). Sunny Seven/Six: Rosamond Wright ("Rosie"; romantic; yellow curls), Carol Lorens (15; new; brother Peter, twins David & Dorothy, parents Mr. & Mrs. Lorens; Chicago loss; Lake Road farmhouse), Betty Burd ("Bettykins"/"Little One"; Uncle George, editor; Mamma; father died), Doris Drexel ("Dory"; Mr. Drexel), Peggy Pierce ("Peg"; mischievous), Bertha Angel ("Burdie"; chairman; grocer father; brother Bob), Gertrude Willis ("Trudie"; minister's daughter; Uncle Pierson; Mr. & Mrs. Willis; Bettykins' tutor). Evelyn Dartmoor (granddaughter of Mr. Dartmoor; collie painting). Mr. Dartmoor (old, shaggy grey brows, cane, "ogre"). Mr. Dickerson (principal). Miss Donovan (8th-grade teacher; left). Mr. Drakely (postman). Uncle Danny (station-master, deaf). Granny Dorset. Dick Jensen (Jensen candy; Jolly Pirates). Jack Doring, Bob Angel, Donald Burnley (Arizona cattle plans). Madame Deriby (Linden Hall matron; silvery hair). Miss Sharpleigh, Miss Merritt (teachers), Miss Berry (kindergarten), Marie (maid), Patrick O'Neil & Billie (stable men), Mr. Haley (riding master), Mr. O'Rourke (farmer, eggs/turkeys), Mr. & Mrs. Diggitt (Elmhurst gardener/lodge). Arthur Ellsworth (~18), Aunt Louise Ellsworth, grandfather A. R. Ellsworth (dead, portrait). Alise Alderly (6; orphan; grandfather Ellsworth). Gladys Merle Jones (Beef King daughter, Chicago, clique), Anita Ryan, Janet Nagel, Jenny Clark. Katrina Mason (spoiled). Matilda "Starr" Perkins (Dakota prairie, 15; mother Margaret Inslay, English; brothers Cedric, Basil; dog Shep; Bishop Wesley). Geraldine Barrington ("Lady Stuckup", English; father Mr. Barrington, Barrington Manor). Eva Dearman (Arizona; Uncle Dick; Amanda Brown m. "Rusty Pete"; baby). Madge & Everett Petersen. Marie Le Clerc (French essay winner). Nina Best. Little Anne. Miss Perring (uniform maker). Professor Patz (piano). Madame Vandeheuton (medal). Mr. Slocum (not in this book).

**Ch 1 – New Sunnysider.** Adele, 8th grade, next year Dorchester High with Jack. Meets Carol Lorens (new; Dorchester High since she's 15). Carol's family: Chicago lawyer father lost fortune, moved to father's boyhood farmhouse on Lake Road, orchard.

**Ch 2 – The Ogre.** Carol's dilemma (Dorchester costly). Mother: had hoped for boarding school (music, drawing). Peter gave up college. Carol errands to Mr. Dartmoor (castle, lions); twins; "Mr. Dartmoor is Santa Claus." Granddaughter Evelyn in Buffalo-area boarding school, lonely; portrait with collie. Carol: "every cloud has silver lining."

**Ch 3 – Two Surprises.** Evelyn's letter ("Dearest Granddad... Madame Deriby insists I have a roommate"). Dartmoor offers Carol place as roommate/companion at Linden Hall Seminary. Dorothy offers to help Mummie. Sunny Seven meet; Adele: "Queer things happen!"

**Ch 4 – New Faces.** Departure; Father: "ask yourself, What would my mother do?" Train 9am; Buffalo 2 hrs + local. Linden station; Evelyn embraces Mr. Dartmoor. Bus ride; Linden Hall: elm drive, pillared colonial house.

**Ch 5 – Letter from Carol.** Carol's letter read by Adele; Madame Deriby description. Miss Donovan's mother ill; she won't return. Mr. Dickerson: Dorchester solution. Secret Sanctum (log cabin). Bertha, Peggy, Doris, Rosie can go; Betty can't (Uncle George); Gertrude stays (father teaching). Adele: "bones are good prophets."

**Ch 6 – Betty's Uncle George.** Betty sad; Uncle George: "Betty Bobbets," "Puss"; will send her; allowance. Madame Deriby's letter: room for 8 more; school bus Saturday 4pm. Gertrude stays (minister's salary).

**Ch 7 – Departure.** Station scene; Uncle Danny; Jack, Bob teasing; Dick Jensen's candy boxes; Jolly Pirates jump on train.

**Ch 8 – Apple-Blossom Alley.** Carol & Evelyn in garden; Adele's letter ("Gertrude... I feel in my bones"). Girls arrive Saturday 4:30. South wing corridor (apple-blossom walls) named Apple-Blossom Alley. Rooms: Rosie & Bertha; Peggy & Doris ("Inseparables"); Adele & Betty; Carol & Evelyn (moved from west wing). Gladys Merle Jones clique described.

**Ch 9 – Gladys Merle's Clique.** Anita Ryan, Janet Nagel, Jenny Clark. Plan to write Anita's aunt (Sunnyside) to check social standing. Gladys slips letter into gate box. Patrick & Billie hear; Billie: "Huh! Nothin' but girls."

**Ch 10 – Downfall.** Aunt's letter read: Carol a paid companion, poor lawyer. Janet defends Carol, deserts Gladys. Gladys snubs Adele; Adele cool. Gladys: father "stately, handsome".

**Ch 11 – True Nobility.** Mr. Jones visits (stout, red-faced, ranchman). Gladys humiliated, sobs. Carol visits; great-grandfather refused royal title; "The Making of Royalty". Gladys apologises; spends day with father.

**Ch 12 – Wish Fulfilled.** Adele interviews with Madame Deriby; Miss Berry leaves (brother ill); Madame wants a young teacher for little ones in exchange for tuition. Adele proposes Gertrude; letter sent.

**Ch 13 – New Teacher.** Gertrude's arrival Saturday; phone from Mr. Willis; train derailed onto siding half-mile away; Patrick drives bus. Evelyn's roses.

**Ch 14 – Orphan Alise.** Gertrude teaches 10 tots (ages 5–7). Alise (golden hair, 6): "let me love you"; Gertrude: "you be little sister." Gertrude tells of Alise's mother (married against stern father; dead; grandfather refused). Elmhurst ride with Mr. Haley; marble statue of young girl resembling Alise; name ALISE ELLSWORTH on pedestal.

**Ch 15 – Grandfather of Alise.** Gertrude sees A. R. Ellsworth trunk at station. Mr. O'Rourke's farm errand (turkeys). Gertrude & Adele ride to Elmhurst; Arthur Ellsworth (18) receives them; grandfather dead; Aunt Louise. Gertrude tells Alise story; Louise: sister's child is Alise Alderly; will visit. Adele: "wish to be acquainted with Ellsworths."

**Ch 16 – Taming Katrina.** Sunny girls meet; Katrina Mason (spoiled, fretful, rude). Madame Deriby asks. Rhyme "Rosies, posies..." picks Carol. Carol's "loving kindness". Carol offers Katrina role of Norah in play (Carol takes summer girl part). Katrina: none like her; idea: share Thanksgiving goodies box.

**Ch 17 – Unexpected Spread.** Party in Katrina's room ("Iceland"). Carol's introductions (mock). Feast on floor: cold turkey, cranberry jelly, chocolate cake. Gertrude invited. Rosie apologises; Katrina: "to-morrow I may forget." Rehearsals daily.

**Ch 18 – Thanksgiving.** Invitation from Ellsworths (Louise: "Dear Miss Gertrude and Miss Adele"). Dinner Thursday 2pm. Chrysanthemums: "At the hour of three A surprise there will be!" Surprise: "Russian" guests Mr. Mellowisky (Bob), Donald Burnley, and Jack in disguise. Arthur wrote Jack; they were schoolmates in Dorchester. Boys meet Madame Deriby. Betty: Arthur likes Gertrude.

**Ch 19 – Just Skipping Along.** Snow; Betty snowballs. Sleigh party at Elmhurst (48 girls); Alise's birthday; Miss Ellsworth. Play: Carol's Norah wins; Katrina summer girl; Katrina gives Carol credit. Midwinter exams; holidays; Jolly Pirates at station. Adele enters French essay contest; Marie Le Clerc wins medal; Adele second. Gladys Merle's birthday theatre party in Buffalo. March: Matilda arrives.

**Ch 20 – Old-Fashioned Pupil.** Peggy describes Matilda Perkins (plaid shawl, beaver cap, mittens, skimpy skirt). Madame Deriby's pupil via Bishop Wesley (old friend; sister schooled with Deriby in France). Only bed: with Geraldine Barrington ("Lady Stuckup"). Mother Margaret Inslay (English; "Ivondale"). Dakota: mother a ranchman's wife, orphaned at 12. Gertrude: Sunnyside Club motto: "The only creed of which we have need is the art of being kind."

**Ch 21 – Prairie Home.** Starr's story: blizzard; Basil and Cedric rescue elderly bishop (Bishop Wesley) with Shep; mother's picture, Bible. Adele lends uniform; names her "Starr" (double r). Geraldine's room; Peggy's cupola-ghost story (Nina Best).

**Ch 22 – Lady Stuckup.** Geraldine cold; Starr lonely, then cheers. Geraldine asks Madame Deriby to move; offered cupola. Starr's diary read by Geraldine (snoops). Peggy's ghost story (Nina Best, cold hand). Starr walks to wood; finds trailing arbutus; finds Geraldine lying with sprained ankle. Starr offers to help; Mr. O'Rourke's wagon takes Geraldine back.

**Ch 23 – Dream Came True.** Geraldine (nursed by Starr): sorry; wants Starr as roommate. Geraldine's father Mr. Barrington (searching for lost sister in West). Starr reveals mother Margaret Inslay; Barrington's sister. Adele: "Cinderella." Adele invites Starr to visit summer.

**Ch 24 – C.E.P.** Closing Exercises Party (night before departure); invitations to boys. Adele's secret: Gertrude's 16th birthday; surprise party. Gertrude's sister-friend plot; Gertrude secret with Arthur.

**Ch 25 – String of Pearls.** Fund: Gertrude wanted pearls; Uncle Pierson's $20 last year bought lilac silk and black suit for Mummie (Gertrude's mother) for Boston convention. Evelyn treasurer. Betty's pink muslin remade by Adele.

**Ch 26 – Romancing.** Adele: "Arizona cattleman." Letters: Eva Dearman coming; Amanda Brown's baby; Donald Burnley to attend; Jack's letter: camping on uncle's island in St. Lawrence in August; Uncle Jack & Aunt Dahlia sailing for Europe.

**Ch 27 – Old Friends Arrive.** Madge Petersen (chaperone) & Everett (sailing). Adele: "I'd like Everett Petersen as Sailor-in-chief." Eva, Madge, Everett arrive; Betty & Adele meet. Everett and Arthur drive away; Madame Deriby: cupola room for guests.

**Ch 28 – Closing Party.** Adele's pink rose in Rosie's hair. Starr: silver star circlet (Geraldine's gift). Hawaiian musicians. Madame Deriby: "lads never admire simpering girls." Gertrude's surprise: girls form circle, sing "Happy birthday to our Gertrude"; Betty presents velvet box: string of "friendship pearls."

**Ch 29 – Bud of a Romance.** Lanterns in orchard; Arthur and Gertrude at table; Arthur proposes courtship; Gertrude: "I'll gladly become your aunt's niece... until then, I would rather not accept help."

**Ch 30 – Farewell, Linden Hall.** Packing; Starr: invite all to prairie home. Adele's farewell to Madame Deriby. Arthur's tally-ho; song "Farewell, Dear Linden Hall." Last line: Adele: "here endeth another chapter..."; Betty: "Adele Doring out camping!"
